title: Selection consensus guardrail for E4M3 / E5M2 FP8 profiles
creator: Avery Kim
description:
Goal: implement a conservative, observable "consensus" mechanism that selects between E4M3 and E5M2 FP8 quantization profiles at runtime and prevents noisy oscillation or silent accuracy regressions. The feature will add a short-term voting window, hysteresis, and cross-batch sanity checks so we safely enable FP8 profiles for Hopper GPUs across different model shapes and customer workloads.

Motivation and scope:
- Many models show workload-dependent preferences between E4M3 and E5M2. A static selector triggers regressions in ~0.5% of real requests (seen in early canaries).
- We need a runtime guard that: (a) collects lightweight per-shard activation stats, (b) computes a consensus over N requests/shards, (c) applies hysteresis and safety thresholds, and (d) emits telemetry + regression signals for automatic rollback.
- Scope includes runtime selector implementation, telemetry schema, calibration harness extension (golden prompts + batch diversity), canary rollout plan, and a QA suite (unit + integration + golden-eval).

Design summary:
1) Voting window: selector aggregates up to 128 inference activations or 10 seconds, whichever comes first. Each activation votes E4M3/E5M2 based on per-op clipping and quant-error metric (L2 residual on float baseline sampled across KV cache prefixes).
2) Consensus rule: require >=65% majority and at least 20 independent activation votes across a minimum of 3 different shards to flip profile.
3) Hysteresis / cooldown: once a profile is chosen, block flips for 5 minutes or until a sustained 90% majority is observed for two consecutive windows.
4) Safety thresholds: abort FP8 activation if averaged token-level perplexity delta > 1.5% on golden prompts or if embed-distance regression exceeds configurable sentinel.
5) Fallback path: automatically fall back to INT8/FP16 equivalent variant if safety checks fail; flag an incident and tag the request for post-mortem sampling.

Calibration & validation plan:
- Extend calibration pipeline to emit per-layer scale stats and a compact fingerprint for each calibration run (sha256 of quant lookup table + per-op histograms). Store fingerprints in S3 and reference them in telemetry.
- Add a golden-eval harness with ~1.2K prompts across short/long tails, heavy prefix reuse, and instruction-following stress cases. Run golden-eval in CI and during canary.
- Create an automated drift detector that compares current golden-eval distributions to historical baseline and raises a regression ticket when drift exceeds 2 sigma.

Observability and alerts:
- New telemetry keys: quant.selector.votes, quant.selector.majority_pct, quant.selector.shards_seen, quant.selector.golden_ppl_delta, quant.selector.embed_delta.
- Dashboard: per-model and per-region breakdown of selection decisions, 1h/24h heatmap, and recent fallback events.
- Alerts: page P0 on >0.2% of requests hitting safety abort in a 5-minute window for commercial customers; otherwise page P1 for internal test fleets.

Canary & rollout strategy:
- Stage 1 (internal): internal dev cluster with synthetic traffic for 72h. Success criteria: no more than 10 safety aborts and no more than 0.1% median latency increase.
- Stage 2 (shadow): route 5% of production traffic shadowed through selector (no user-visible change) for 48h. Run golden-eval every 6h.
- Stage 3 (gradual enable): 0.5% of traffic enabled for FP8 with selector active, ramp to 10% across 7 days if no regressions. Automated rollback triggers on safety thresholds.

Testing and QA:
- Unit tests for voting logic, hysteresis, and fingerprint generation.
- Integration tests in the runtime test harness (multi-shard replay of recorded traces).
- Perf benchmark: measure token/sec and p95 latency vs baseline (FP16) on Hopper A100-equivalent nodes.

Acceptance criteria (must pass to mark Done):
- Selector implemented in runtime and covered by unit/integration tests.
- Golden-eval shows no statistically significant regression vs baseline for the targeted canary traffic.
- Telemetry keys ingested and dashboard created.
- Canary run completed without automated rollback for 7 continuous days on the internal + shadow stages.
- Confluence doc and runbook updated with rollback/playbook steps.
